about: The work that remains, one item per gap, in the order it is planned (decision 0016). Rendered into Docs/TODO.md and the progress page by scripts/gen-progress.py; edit this file, never the outputs. `priority`: next (Phase 8, in order) | soon (the gap sweep after it: what ordinary apps hit) | later (needs a decision, a new subsystem or a platform that does not exist yet). `status`: planned | in-progress | done (with the date) | wontfix (a documented non-goal, with the reason in `detail`). `kind`: missing (no API) | accepted (API compiles, no behaviour) | approximate (behaves, pixels or motion differ) | verify (behaves, never measured against Apple) | infra (tooling, docs, site). Move an item to done when its support row changes; keep it here so the page shows what landed.

items.title: One source of truth for what works and what is next
items.detail: scripts/gen-progress.py validates Docs/todo.json and Docs/support.json (a framework per section, a fixture or a noFixture reason per row that does something, fixtures that exist, a generated date) and renders Docs/TODO.md, Docs/support-matrix.md and the landing page's SupportData.swift; support-matrix.py and gen-landing-support.py are gone; CI --check fails on stale outputs.

items.title: Support rows for every UIKit class
items.detail: Ten UIKit sections (views and layers, controls, text, containers, navigation and bars, presentation, Auto Layout, drawing, animation, app and events), 48 rows with a status, notes and the uikit/ and ios/representable fixtures that prove each; the matrix shows per-framework counts.

items.title: Audit the stale rows and doc notes
items.detail: Reconciled 2026-09-18: the Phase 0 notes on the composition rows and the stacks, the Transaction row (animation exists), Text.md's kerning and underline row, Animation.md's not-yet list, and the first Open lines of CollectionView.md, Presentation.md, TableView.md and Navigation.md.

items.title: A live example for every support row
items.detail: Every SwiftUI row that does something names fixtures now (state rows to button/, toggle/, foreach/ and observable/, composition rows to layout/ and customlayout/), demo/pasteboard joins the golden-less prefixes, and three rows say why no fixture can exist (previews, content transitions, windows).

items.title: Publish the gallery next to the landing page
items.detail: scripts/build-landing.sh builds a release Examples/Gallery into dist/gallery/ next to the landing page (3.53 MB brotli at the first release build; the deploy refuses more than 4 MB), with the landing page's loading screen, a link back to the site, `?filter=<prefix>` narrowing the list and showing the first match, and the size line in the log; the landing workflow rebuilds on gallery and fixture changes.

items.title: The progress page
items.detail: Examples/Progress, a SwiftUI app at /progress/: counts per framework, the full matrix with a search field and status filters, every row linking to its gallery fixtures, the todo list grouped by priority and framework with links to the docs, what landed recently and the non-goals; ProgressData.swift is generated by scripts/gen-progress.py and checked by CI; built into the site by scripts/build-landing.sh behind a 3 MB gate.

items.title: The landing page links to progress and examples
items.detail: The landing page's navigation bar, hero and footer link to /progress/ and /gallery/; the matrix section is a summary card (rows per framework and status, generated) with buttons to the full page and the gallery, which drops the row blob from the landing bundle; README and the docs point at the same two pages.

items.title: The element workflow records progress
items.detail: ELEMENT_WORKFLOW step 6: update the support row (a fixture or a noFixture reason, the generated date), mark the todo item done with the date, add the new gaps as items, run scripts/gen-progress.py and commit its outputs, add the roadmap status row; the landing workflow redeploys the site on every push to main that touches the data, the pages or the runtime.

items.title: layoutOptions and safe areas through the seam
items.detail: `_PlatformViewRepresentableLayoutOptions` (`propagatesSafeArea`, the default): a representable's UIKit tree gets the part of its frame under a SwiftUI bar or inset as its window's safe area, and `UIHostingController.safeAreaRegions` hands the controller's safe area (a navigation or tab bar's) to the hosted runtime. Measured on the simulator under a navigation bar (ios/representable/safearea*, hostingsafearea*), with the safe area's geometric rule for every view (Position.md).

items.title: Environment to trait collection
items.detail: colorScheme is userInterfaceStyle, dynamicTypeSize the content size category, layoutDirection and the size classes follow through `UITraitOverrides`; `updateUIView` runs when they change (ios/representable/traits, ios/dark/representable-controls).

items.title: Hover inside a representable
items.detail: SwiftUI's pointer moves reach the hosted tree as a hover (`UIHoverGestureRecognizer` events) and the hovered view's `UIPointerInteraction` style or a button's pointer effect becomes the host cursor (ios/representable/hover, Playwright/representable-hover-probe.mjs, RepresentableTests).

items.title: Wheel scrolling of a hosted UIScrollView
items.detail: ios/representable/wheel (a UIScrollView in a representable inside a SwiftUI ScrollView) and Playwright/wheel-probe.mjs: a wheel over the inner scroll view moves it by the delta while the outer holds; past its end the outer takes the rest.

items.title: Animations across the seam
items.detail: `context.transaction` carries the SwiftUI animation into `updateUIView`; a `withAnimation` that resizes a representable lays the UIKit view out at every tweened size; `UIView.animate` inside `updateUIView` runs on the outer clock, advanced once per host frame for every representable. `RepresentableTests` on the headless clock.

items.title: Representables in lists, forms, scroll views and sheets
items.detail: ios/representable/list, form and scroll on the simulator: row heights and the hosted views' frames exact (a header-less grouped section sits 35 below the previous card, which the runtime now does). A representable in a sheet joins sw-ios-sheets.

items.title: Dismantle and coordinator lifecycle tests
items.detail: `RepresentableTests` and ios/representable/lifecycle: make, update, dismantle order at first sight, on an identity change (the new coordinator, view and update come before the old view's dismantle) and on removal; every evaluation of the parent's body updates the view; the coordinator is made once per node, outlives updates and dies with the node.

items.title: UIHostingConfiguration: margins, self-sizing, configuration state
items.detail: Measured on the simulator (ios/representable/hostingmargins, hostingcollection, hostingstate): default margins 15 above and below, a table row's fit plus its separator point, self-sizing collection list cells exactly the fit, and the cell's configuration state (`configurationUpdateHandler`, `updateConfiguration(using:)`, `setNeedsUpdateConfiguration`, now in UIKitWeb for table and collection cells) rebuilding the hosted content on selection.

items.title: UIHostingController in containers
items.detail: ios/representable/hostingnav, hostingsizing and UIHostingControllerTests: a hosting controller under a navigation or tab bar sees the bars' safe area (ix-layout-options); navigationTitle and toolbar items drive its navigationItem as titled bar buttons whose taps run the actions; sizingOptions keep the preferred size and invalidate the intrinsic size; rootView set under withAnimation tweens. A representable is re-measured only when its value, environment or proposal changes.

items.title: Image(uiImage:) for rendered images
items.detail: ios/representable/renderedimage: a UIImage from UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawn by Image (at its size, resizable, as a template in the foreground colour; withTintColor alone keeps the colours, as measured), and pngData() rasterised by the host (a canvas in the browser, CoreGraphics natively).

items.title: The unmeasured sizing corners
items.detail: Done 2026-09-18: `ios/representable/measure-controls`, `measure-baselines`, `measure-axes` and `grid` on the simulator; the segmented control's 31 pt alignment rect and 32 pt minimum segment, sliders and progress views hugging vertically, the compact date picker's missing intrinsic size, label baselines at 12/20/34 pt, one-axis intrinsic sizes and a Grid with representables (Docs/elements/Representable.md).

items.title: Decide whether SwiftUI keeps re-exporting UIKit unconditionally
items.detail: Decided 2026-09-18 (decision 0014, size gate outcome): the re-export stays unconditional; Counter is 3,046,910 bytes brotli against the 3,145,728 budget after the representable work (97 KB of headroom), so uk-size follows next to win at least 300 KB back.

items.title: NSViewRepresentable and NSViewControllerRepresentable
items.detail: Apps written for the macOS profile reach for AppKit representables; there is no AppKitWeb to host them. Out of scope until a decision says whether an AppKitWeb is worth building or the API should compile as an empty view; recorded here so the choice is visible.

items.title: iOS sheets, tab bars and date pickers from the simulator

List rows outside a ForEach now take their identity from `tag`.

items.title: iOS presentations and bars: the rest

The macOS looks stay approximate in the support row: sheets, popovers and alerts are separate windows the harness cannot capture; a window-list capture spike would measure them (sw-mac-presentation-looks).

items.title: Measure the macOS presentation looks
items.detail: The sheet, popover, alert and menu looks on macOS are by eye (separate windows the golden harness cannot capture). A window-list capture (CGWindowListCreateImage over the app's windows after a step presents) in the AppKit golden host would pin the panel geometry, materials and shadows the way `capturesWindow` does on iOS.

items.title: List editing: onDelete, onMove, swipe actions, refreshable

Rest in sw-list-editing-rest.

items.title: List editing: the rest

items.title: List styles, spacing and outline forms
items.detail: Done 2026-09-19: eight fixtures (macOS 26.6 goldens for alternating rows, header prominence, outlines, item tints, section separators, a hidden scroll background and the pinned header while scrolling; ios/list/spacing on the simulator). List(_:children:), OutlineGroup and DisclosureGroup rows, listRowSpacing/listSectionSpacing, alternatingRowBackgrounds, scrollContentBackground, listItemTint and listSectionSeparator work; the focused accent look and lazy rows stay open (sw-list-looks-rest).

items.title: List looks: the rest
items.detail: The focused accent selection (the golden window is never key), lazy rows, listRowHoverEffect, the pinned header's gradient shadow, ListSectionSpacing.compact, the section separator tint macOS draws grey, a header-less card's custom section spacing on iOS (derived, not measured), outline chevron presses limited to the chevron.

items.title: Scroll position, targets and geometry
items.detail: Done 2026-09-19: scrollPosition (id and ScrollPosition bindings), scrollTargetLayout, scrollTargetBehavior (paging, viewAligned with limits, custom behaviours), contentMargins, onScrollGeometryChange, onScrollPhaseChange, defaultScrollAnchor(for:) roles, scrollIndicatorsFlash, scrollDismissesKeyboard (iOS), ScrollViewReader inside List; six macOS goldens (26.6) and two simulator twins measure the position binding, margins, geometry and anchor roles; the overlay scroller knob was measured from NSScroller.drawKnob.

items.title: Real laziness and pinned headers
items.detail: Done 2026-09-19: a ForEach in a lazy stack or grid inside a scroll view creates its elements as they come within a viewport of the visible region (placeholders sized by the created ones keep the content's extent; scrollTo creates its target), pinnedViews pins section headers and footers (six macOS goldens: lazy/pinned-headers, -footers, -both, laziness, grid-sections, grid-alignment), sections in grids take their own lines, GridItem alignment against the grid's measured (no change needed). Elements are kept rather than released.

items.title: TextField forms and the painted caret
items.detail: Done 2026-10-03: TextField(_:value:format:) and formatter: (committing on Return or blur; number/percent/currency styles and NumberFormatter on wasm through WebFoundation), onEditingChanged/onCommit, axis: .vertical (wrapping, lineLimit, reserved lines; a textarea in the browser), submitLabel, textContentType, keyboardType, textInputAutocapitalization and autocorrectionDisabled reaching the input element, the caret and selection painted into the display list; goldens textfield/vertical, textfield/formatted (plain style, macOS 26.6) and ios/textfield/vertical; the iPhone reserved-lines height stays approximate.

items.title: allowsTightening and minimumScaleFactor
items.detail: Done 2026-10-03: minimumScaleFactor shrinks a line that would truncate to the largest fitting scale (a five-step search down to the minimum, then truncation at the minimum); allowsTightening closes the letter spacing up to a 72nd of the size per character before truncating; measured on text/fit (two factors, five widths, a title, tightening alone and combined, a two-line paragraph); the recorded engine keys both so Tier A is exact, pixels within the loosened bound.

items.title: AttributedString, markdown, dates and images in Text
items.detail: Done 2026-10-03: markdown in string literals (bold, italic, code, strikethrough, links, escapes; _InlineMarkdown in WebFoundation), Text(AttributedString) with the SwiftUI attribute scope (font, colours, decorations, baseline offset, kern, tracking) plus Foundation's link and inlinePresentationIntent (a WebFoundation AttributedString stand-in on wasm with init(markdown:)), Text(Image) laid out as a symbol glyph on the baseline, Text(date, style:) (date, time at the environment's time zone; relative, offset and timer re-resolving each second) and Text(_:format:), links in text that open through openURL and show the hand; four macOS goldens, Tier A exact. Open: DateInterval and ranges, Duration, per-run kern, backgroundColor painting, non-system inline images.

items.title: Custom fonts
items.detail: Done 2026-10-03: Font.custom with a bundled font file: scripts/assets.py reads every ttf/otf under the source (names, head/hhea/OS2/post metrics) into the manifest and copies the file; the browser loads a FontFace and relayouts when it arrives, the native host, the pixel tier and the harness register the file with CoreText; the layouter's line is the rounded ascent plus the rounded descent (measured at twenty sizes); the recorded engine keys the family (custom:Name:size:weight). Fixture text/custom-font with Abel (OFL). Open: dynamic-type scaling of relativeTo, variable fonts, UIFont(name:) in UIKitWeb.

items.title: Dynamic Type
items.detail: `dynamicTypeSize` and the content size categories: the text-style tables at every category (measured on the simulator), `ScaledMetric`, the environment from the host's setting.

items.title: TextEditor: selection, find, long content
items.detail: A selection binding, `findNavigator`/`findDisabled`/`replaceDisabled`, `lineLimit` on editors, scrolling of long content, and the NSTextView wrapping parity (texteditor/basic is approximate).

items.title: Selecting text
items.detail: `textSelection(.enabled)` only sets the I-beam: drag selection over painted text, copy, the selection highlight in the display list, on both hosts.

items.title: NavigationStack gaps
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: navigationDestination(item:) (push, swap in place, pop both ways), NavigationPath.CodableRepresentation with init(_:) and codable (mangled type names and JSON, last first), ⌘[ and Escape popping the stack around the focused control, and the measured stack layout (the frame is the top screen's size, screens centre in the largest screen's box; a presented screen survives a path change under it, so the entry removal the item described is not SwiftUI's behaviour). macOS back button and push animation stay open (window chrome).

items.title: Scroll content under the iOS 26 bar
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04 (approximate): measured on the simulator with ios/nav/list-scroll and ios/nav/ignores. A scroll view ignoring the top safe area keeps its safe probe frame while its content starts at the window's top and a scrollTo lands at y 0; the collapse then shifts no offset (fixed). A List under the large title scrolls under the glass and collapses the bar like a scroll view, but UIKit re-anchors the targeted row after the collapse (row 1 at 9.25, row 8 at 15.75 under the inline bar) by a rule not pinned down: those rows are compared only before the steps.

items.title: NavigationSplitView chrome
items.detail: The sidebar's material and toolbar, dragging the divider, collapsing by drag, the styles (accepted), `preferredCompactColumn` in the iOS profile; the splitview/ fixtures out of the 9 % approximate bound.

items.title: The Tab API, page style and badges
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: the Tab API (titles, system and catalog images, values, custom labels, TabContent), badge(_:) on tabs (the iOS red capsule measured on ios/tabs/badges with five tabs), disabled tabs (no press, skipped by the arrow keys), tabViewStyle(.page) (pages side by side, a swipe turns them, the dots measured on ios/tabs/page) and the other styles accepted; tabview/tab-api on macOS 26.6 (frames exact; the selected segment's new raised look stays open with the 26.2 goldens).

items.title: Menu rows, sections and navigation
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04 (approximate: macOS opens menus in windows the goldens cannot capture): Toggle rows with check marks, Picker options as checked rows, Section headers as small secondary rows, Label icons through the label style, hover highlight of the row under the pointer, menuOrder accepted, menuActionDismissBehavior (.disabled keeps the menu open), contextMenu(forSelectionType:) on List (the clicked row or the selection), the split button's and pull-down's open look; keyboard navigation was already in place.

items.title: Picker options and looks
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: Picker(sources:selection:) (shared value, writes to every source, mixed sources select nothing), tag(_:includeOptional:), image and Label options shown as themselves in segments and pop-ups, dividers and section headers in the pop-up's menu, the focused accent ring of the segmented control (approximate), keyboard navigation (already present); palette stays the menu style and the pop-up's open look unmeasured. macOS 26.6 changed picker sizing (stretch to the proposal, 20/22 pt controls), recorded in the doc and kept out of the goldens.

items.title: Toolbar modifiers with an effect
items.detail: `toolbarBackground`, `toolbarRole`, `toolbarTitleDisplayMode` (accepted today), `toolbar(id:)` customisation, `ToolbarCommands`, sheet toolbars, a real `NSToolbar` in the native host.

items.title: Search suggestions, scopes and tokens
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: searchable(text:isPresented:) (the presentation is the field's focus), searchable(text:tokens:) with token tags, searchSuggestions shown (iOS: a plain accent-coloured list replacing the content; macOS: a menu under the toolbar's field, approximate), searchCompletion (text and token), searchScopes with activation (iOS: a 44 pt band with a 32 pt segmented control under the hidden bar; macOS: a 30 pt row under the toolbar, approximate), searchPresentationToolbarBehavior, isSearching following the presentation; iOS 26's bottom search field measured on the simulator (ios/search/basic, active, tokens: Tier A exact, Tier C about 1 %). searchToolbarBehavior(.minimize), suggestedTokens and navigationBarDrawer accepted without effect.

items.title: Window commands, dragging and documents
items.detail: `commands` on scenes and a menu bar in the native host, dragging and resizing the in-host windows, per-window focus and keyboard routing, `DocumentGroup`, restoration, the accepted scene modifiers (`windowResizability`, `windowStyle`, `defaultPosition`).

items.title: Button roles, sizes and states
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: PrimitiveButtonStyle with its configuration and trigger(), controlSize bezels (ios/button/looks measured on the simulator: mini and small 31 pt capsules of a subheadline label, large and extra large 54.5 pt capsules; macOS approximate from 26.6's differences), the destructive role (iOS measured; macOS the same, unverified), the disabled looks (iOS measured; macOS 26.6's 30 % label and the plain 50 %), the focus ring already drawn by the runtime, hover unchanged; the pressed look stays unverified. button/looks on macOS 26.6 (white 20 pt bezels, no accent in an inactive window) is documented and kept out of the golden set.

items.title: Toggle sources, mixed state and looks
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: Toggle(sources:isOn:) with isMixed (a dash; a flip writes every source), Space and Return through the generic activation, the focus ring around the control only (_FocusRingProviding), controlSize checkboxes and switches (approximate: 26.6's differences shifted onto the 26.2 goldens), tint (the iOS switch's on track; macOS in an active window), the switch knob's shadow from toggle/styles pixels, the active-window accent checkbox and switch behind Runtime.windowIsActive (off by default); hover changes nothing on macOS. toggle/looks on macOS 26.6 is documented and kept out of the golden set.

items.title: Slider styles and stepper repeat
items.detail: `sliderStyle`, tick labels, vertical sliders, the knob shadow; the stepper's press-and-hold repeat and its `formatter`/`format` forms.

items.title: Animated progress and gauges
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: the spinner steps its dark spoke clockwise (one revolution a second) and the indeterminate bar's segment crosses the track every 1.5 s (frame subscriptions; approximate, the goldens keep their first frames), animated values under withAnimation for the bar, the ring and the gauges, ProgressView(timerInterval:countsDown:) through the animation timeline with an m:ss current value label, ProgressView(_ progress:) (wasm's Progress is SwiftUIWebCore's observable object; Foundation's is polled every frame), tint (the iOS fill; macOS in an active window). Marked gauge value labels stay accepted and undrawn, as on macOS.

items.title: DatePicker editing and calendars
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: typing digits into the selected component (Delete, A/P), the compact style's popover calendar on macOS, days outside the range dimmed (datepicker/looks, 26.6 draws the calendar as 26.2 did) and inert, dragging the clock's hands, the iOS wheel style measured on the simulator (ios/datepicker/wheel: a cylinder of 23 pt rows; approximate), locale formats for the field (en_GB, de_DE, fr_FR, ja_JP, nl from datepicker/locales on 26.6, out of the golden set), both graphical components 18 apart. Other calendars and localised names stay out.

items.title: A real colour panel
items.detail: The browser's `<input type=color>` and the native colour panel behind the well (the preset popover stands in, unverified), a `CGColor` binding, keyboard activation, dropping colours.

items.title: Context-dependent labels and formatted values
items.detail: `Label`'s automatic style by context (icon only in toolbars), multi-line titles, `LabeledContent(_:value:format:)`, the secondary value colour in grouped forms (unmeasured).

items.title: Disclosure animation and outlines
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: the row's press toggles under the default animation (the group's frames tween, the content fades in or out through .transition(.opacity); a binding changed outside a transaction snaps); outline rows in lists were done with sw-list-looks (2026-09-19); the chevron stays the measured stroke (Tier C 0.04 %) rather than the symbol glyph.

items.title: Grouped form constants
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: the grouped form measured on macOS 26.6 (which lays it out as 26.2 did): headers in the semibold body font 10 above their card, footers in the 13 pt font right-aligned 10 below, cards 10 apart and a header 30 after a section, rows their content plus 20 with no minimum, the picker and stepper rows (form/grouped, in the golden set), a GroupBox bare inside a card, a nested columns form as a row, scrollContentBackground(.hidden) (form/grouped-background); the slider and button rows and the 26.6 card look (4/255 fill, hairline) recorded in the doc, the small switch left as measured on 26.2.

items.title: ContentUnavailableView in containers
items.detail: Inside lists and navigation, the iOS vertical centring, the symbol above the title on other platforms.

items.title: ShareLink items and previews
items.detail: `Transferable` items, `SharePreview`, `message`; the browser's `navigator.share` and the native sharing service picker behind it; hover looks for `Link`.

items.title: ViewThatFits
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: ViewThatFits(in:content:) picks the first candidate whose ideal size fits the proposal on the constrained axes (the last otherwise), laying out, painting and probing only it; layout/view-that-fits measures a grid of widths and heights and both axis sets (Tier A exact, Tier C 0.00 %).

items.title: Right-to-left layout direction
items.detail: `layoutDirection` through stacks, grids, custom layouts, `layoutDirectionBehavior` on shapes, alignment guides and the text layouter; goldens from a right-to-left locale.

items.title: Layout protocol corners
items.detail: `Layout.Animatable` (animating layout parameters), `updateCache` reuse across passes and invalidation on environment changes, `GridLayout` as a `Layout` value, rows with more cells than the widest earlier row combined with spans.

items.title: Shape corners: strokedPath, container shapes, roles
items.detail: `Path.strokedPath` as the offset outline (polygons per segment today), `ContainerRelativeShape` following its container, `Shape.role` (stub), `Path(cgPath:)` on Apple platforms.

items.title: Canvas images, symbols and filters
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: draw(Image) and resolve(Image) through image nodes, resolveSymbol over the tagged symbols child, addFilter (blur, shadow, colour matrices) and blendMode wrapping each operation in display-list groups, tiledImage shadings, withCGContext as a scratch context on Apple platforms, the renderer under observation tracking so state it reads repaints; canvas/images Tier A exact, Tier C 0.56 %.

items.title: Elliptical and mesh gradients
items.detail: `EllipticalGradient`, `MeshGradient`, `ShapeStyle.in(_:)`, gradient `opacity`, repeat and mirror options (accepted), gradients on images and symbols, the hierarchical fade levels (approximate).

items.title: Animated effects and drawing groups
items.detail: Effect values under animation, `drawingGroup(opaque:colorMode:)` (accepted), filtering of content painted outside its frame, `drawingGroup`'s rasterisation semantics.

items.title: 3D and projection transforms
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: rotation3DEffect and projectionEffect paint the affine part of their matrices about the anchor (perspective accepted, not drawn), GeometryEffect conformances through View.modifier with animatable data tweened under an animation, hit testing mapped back through every effect's transform (hitTestTransform), scale transitions about their anchor; transform/3d (a depth-axis turn, a projection, a custom skew) exact, the x and y turns unit-tested because the harness cannot capture them.

items.title: SF Symbols fidelity
items.detail: Lucide stands in for every glyph: rendering modes (accepted), multicolour and hierarchical layers, `variableValue`, sizes and names beyond the 240 measured (a full metrics table from the catalog goldens), symbol effects by layer; decision needed on a symbol source with a licence that allows shipping.

items.title: Image catalog forms and rendering
items.detail: PDF and SVG catalog sets, slicing metadata, dark-appearance image variants, Display P3 (used as sRGB), `Image(size:label:renderer:)`, `luminanceToAlpha` and `colorMultiply` on images, redaction placeholders for catalog images (approximate).

items.title: AsyncImage caching and transactions
items.detail: Cancellation on unmount, a cache keyed by URL, the phase transaction (accepted), the default placeholder colour (approximate).

items.title: Safe area corners
items.detail: `GeometryProxy.safeAreaInsets`, `safeAreaInset` applied per list element, scroll indicators stopping at the inset; the keyboard region is a documented non-region in a browser. `ignoresSafeArea` on a view whose safe-area modifier hugs it on every edge extends on every edge by the geometric rule (PositionTests): a consequence, not a measurement.

items.title: Animation completion, blending and reduce motion
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: withAnimation(_:completionCriteria:_:completion:) and Transaction.addAnimationCompletion (the runtime that animates claims and fires them by duration or by removal), springs with initialVelocity (blendDuration accepted; retargeting already starts from the presented value), accessibilityReduceMotion wired from the canvas host's prefers-reduced-motion media query (the other accessibility settings are false), exiting ghosts painted by List, Picker and grouped Form, and symbol images crossfading under contentTransition(.symbolEffect/.opacity/.interpolate).

items.title: onReceive, scene phase and URLs
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: onReceive over a Combine-free Publisher protocol (Just, PassthroughSubject, CurrentValueSubject, objectWillChange, $published values, Timer.publish through a main-actor task, NotificationCenter.publisher; wasm stand-ins for Timer, RunLoop, NotificationCenter, Notification and NSUserActivity in WebFoundation), scenePhase from the canvas host's visibilitychange/focus/blur, onOpenURL for the page URL's fragment at launch and hashchange/popstate, onContinueUserActivity through Runtime.continueUserActivity, and children's onAppear before their parents' (verified).

items.title: The @Entry macro
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: `@Entry` in SwiftUIWebMacros (an accessor and peer macro: a private key type named after the property, accessors over the container's subscript, errors outside EnvironmentValues/FocusedValues/Transaction extensions); FocusedValues built for it (FocusedValueKey, focusedValue, focusedSceneValue, @FocusedValue, @FocusedBinding, the runtime composes the focused node's ancestry under the scene values and invalidates readers when focus moves).

items.title: Timeline modes and pausing
items.detail: `lowFrequency` (accepted), pausing when the page is hidden, content reading the environment's calendar and time zone.

items.title: Rendering previews
items.detail: A macro that keeps the `#Preview` body so the gallery can show an app's previews, `PreviewModifier`, `previewLayout`, `previewDisplayName`; the traits are stubs today.

items.title: Simultaneous, pinch and rotate gestures
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: simultaneousGesture as true simultaneity (the pressed node's simultaneousGesture ancestors share the press), GestureMask honoured, the updating body's and the reset closure's transactions applied to @GestureState, MagnifyGesture/RotateGesture (and the older two) from control-wheel pinches, Safari gesture events and two touches through HostedScene.pinch and Runtime.pinch (gesture/pinch, the probe pinches all three ways); onTapGesture counts were already in place (tested).

items.title: Focused values, sections and commands
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: FocusedValue and @FocusedBinding (with sw-entry-macro), focusSection in the Tab order, defaultFocus after mounting, focusScope/prefersDefaultFocus/resetFocus, focus restored after a presentation closes, onCommand with the edit keys as standard selectors, onCopyCommand/onCutCommand/onPasteCommand through NSItemProviders (wasm stand-ins for Selector, NSItemProvider and CharacterSet), onKeyPress(characters:), key-up phases from the host's keyup, type-to-select and ⌘/⇧ clicks in lists; the focus ring measured from AppKit (3 pt, keyboardFocusIndicatorColor at 50 %).

items.title: Custom actions, rotors and a VoiceOver session
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: accessibilityAction (kinds, named, labelled, from buttons), accessibilityAdjustableAction, accessibilitySortPriority, accessibilityHeading levels, live regions, help as the description, accessibilityRepresentation and accessibilityChildren (a second subtree laid out over the view), @AccessibilityFocusState, rotors as navigation landmarks, custom content; accessibility/actions pins the layout and the probe reads Chromium's accessibility tree. The VoiceOver and IME sessions by hand stay with pf-browser-sessions.

items.title: Contrast and per-presentation schemes
items.detail: `colorSchemeContrast`, `preferredColorScheme` per presentation, gauge and date picker chrome verified in dark, the focus ring in dark.

items.title: Hover effects on controls
items.detail: `hoverEffect` and the hovered looks of macOS controls (none change today), the tooltip's measured look.

items.title: Drags across the app boundary
items.detail: Drags to and from the browser page (`DataTransfer`) and other native apps (`NSDraggingSession`), `FileRepresentation`, `dropDestination` on `List` rows with insertion indices, `exportableToServices`, `importsItemProviders`.

items.title: Table columns, styles and interaction
items.detail: `TableColumnForEach`, column groups, `TableRow` builders, `tableStyle`, `tableColumnHeaders`, `alternatingRowBackgrounds`, disclosure rows, column resizing by drag, row context menus, horizontal scrolling of overflowing columns, scrolling rows; the band look (approximate).

items.title: Subviews-based ForEach and Group
items.detail: `ForEach(subviews:)`, `ForEach(sections:)`, `Group(subviews:)`, `containerValues`; the iOS 18 container APIs.

items.title: Charts, Map, VideoPlayer, WebView
items.detail: Separate Apple frameworks. `Charts` is the one apps reach for most and could be a package of its own over the display list; `Map` would need a tile source; `VideoPlayer` and `WebView` need DOM elements under the canvas. Decision needed before any of them starts.

items.title: Image(nsImage:) and Image(cgImage:)
items.detail: No CGImage or NSImage exists on wasm; `Image(cgImage:)` could work natively only. Non-goal for the browser; the native painter may add it with the AppKit decision (ix-appkit).

items.title: onDrag / onDrop with NSItemProvider
items.detail: NSItemProvider and NSString do not exist on wasm; `draggable`/`dropDestination` are the portable forms. Non-goal.

items.title: UIActivityIndicatorView spins
items.detail: Done 2026-09-18: `startAnimating` registers the view with the scene, whose frame loop advances a clock; the spoke pattern steps one spoke every 1/8 s (a revolution per second, approximate: UIKit's rate is not measured) and `stopAnimating`/`hidesWhenStopped` hide it; the goldens keep the still at phase 0 (`ActivityIndicatorTests`).

items.title: Hover and pointer interactions
items.detail: `UIHoverGestureRecognizer`, `UIInteraction` / `UIPointerInteraction` with `UIPointerStyle` (shapes and effects mapped to the cursors a browser can show), `UIButton.isPointerInteractionEnabled`; press-less pointer moves hover the view under them (HoverTests). The pointer's own morphing over a hover-effect view is not drawn.

items.title: Pinch, rotation, swipe and edge pans
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: UISwipeGestureRecognizer, UIScreenEdgePanGestureRecognizer, UIPinchGestureRecognizer and UIRotationGestureRecognizer (from UIKitScene.pinch), TouchRouter.arbitrate honouring the delegate's simultaneous-recognition and failure-requirement methods plus require(toFail:) across all recognizers (an undecided requirement counts as failed at the touch's end); actions no longer report failures (Docs/elements/UIKit/Gestures.md, GestureTests).

items.title: Interactive pop, large-title collapse, custom transitions
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: the interactive pop on a left-edge pan (the screens follow the finger; past half the width or fast completes), the large title collapsing once the top screen's scroll view passes its height and expanding back at the top (SwiftUI's iOS model), titleView sizing from its intrinsic size within the room between items, hidesBottomBarWhenPushed hiding the tab bar for pushed controllers, UIViewControllerTransitioningDelegate / UIViewControllerAnimatedTransitioning / UIViewControllerContextTransitioning for presentations and the navigation delegate's animator for pushes (NavigationPolishTests); the appearance objects stay accepted.

items.title: Tab bar badges and the More tab
items.detail: `UITabBarItem.badgeValue`, the More tab past five items, `UITabBarAppearance` (accepted), tab bar customisation.

items.title: Sheet detents, popovers and custom presentations
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: UISheetPresentationController (detents with medium measured on the simulator, custom resolvers, the grabber, preferredCornerRadius, animateChanges), UIPopoverPresentationController (an arrowed card above or below its source when the delegate keeps it a popover, the page sheet otherwise), action sheets anchored to a source view or bar button item, the adaptive delegates' dismissal callbacks, UIPresentationController subclasses accepted; uikit/sheet/medium (fitted to a hundredth), uikit/popover/basic, uikit/popover/adapted and uikit/alert/anchored measured. The alert severity badge is Mac Catalyst only (accepted).

items.title: Share and document pickers
items.detail: `UIActivityViewController` over `navigator.share` and the native sharing picker; `UIDocumentPickerViewController` over the browser's file input and `NSOpenPanel`; `UIImagePickerController` likewise. What the host cannot offer is documented per host.

items.title: UIMenu presentation
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: UIMenu trees (UIMenuElement, UIAction attributes and states, UIDeferredMenuElement, inline sections, submenus opened in place) presented as a floating card by MenuPresenter for UIButton.menu (showsMenuAsPrimaryAction, changesSelectionAsPrimaryAction, long presses), UIBarButtonItem(menu:), UIContextMenuInteraction (long press, the configuration's preview above the card) and UIEditMenuInteraction (a capsule bar above the point); the card is approximate, as the harness cannot open menus on the simulator (Docs/elements/UIKit/Menus.md, MenuTests).

items.title: UIButton images, subtitles and states
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: measured on the simulator (uikit/button/looks): custom titles are 18 pt in a 34 pt button, images sit in 28 × 20 slots beside or above body titles (system buttons: 22 × 23.5 slots 2 in, 3 to a 15 pt title), subtitles are the footnote 2 under a leading-aligned title, mini and small sizes use the subheadline in 6 × 10 insets and large the body in 15 × 20, pressed fills are at 75 %, disabled ones the tertiary fill under the tertiary label, iOS 26's corners (capsules up to 20 pt, large capsules), the gray style's label-coloured title; configurationUpdateHandler, setNeedsUpdateConfiguration, updateConfiguration, Configuration.updated(for:).

items.title: UILabel attributed text and fitting
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: attributedText with per-range fonts and colours on one baseline (wasm stand-ins for NSAttributedString/NSMutableAttributedString with ranges; rich entries in the recorded metrics), adjustsFontSizeToFitWidth scaling continuously to the width down to minimumScaleFactor (then truncating), allowsDefaultTighteningForTruncation through the engine, the ink position of text-style lines verified against uikit/label/basic's pixels (within half a point); uikit/label/fitting measured.

items.title: Custom, italic and monospaced fonts; Dynamic Type
items.detail: Done 2026-10-04: UIFont(name:size:) from the asset catalog's bundled files (metrics from the font tables; the UIKit harness registers Fixtures/Fonts), italicSystemFont and monospacedSystemFont measured, preferredFont(forTextStyle:compatibleWith:) at every content size category with the styles' own metrics recorded per category (font-metrics.json scaledTextStyles, keyed style:<name>:<category>), UIFontMetrics scaling (one measured point: 16 → 19 at XXL), UILabel.adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory with UIKitScene.preferredContentSizeCategory propagating trait changes; uikit/label/fonts measured. Open: reading the host's text size setting.

items.title: UITextField borders, buttons and views
items.detail: The `line` and `bezel` borders, the clear button, `leftView`/`rightView`, attributed placeholders, the text's vertical position verified against the simulator's pixels, the keyboard types reaching the overlay input. Done 2026-10-04: the line (30 pt, 1 pt label stroke, text 2 in) and bezel (32 pt, 1 pt black 50 % with an inner 33 % line top and left, text 7 in and 1.5 down) borders, the text baseline on the pixel grid, the 17 pt clear button 15 from the right edge with the text ending 11 before it (tapping clears through textFieldShouldClear), leftView/rightView flush to the edges and centred with their modes, attributedPlaceholder in its font and colour, keyboardType/returnKeyType/autocapitalizationType/autocorrectionType/textContentType reaching the input element (UITextView too); uikit/textfield/looks with an edit step (Tier A exact, Tier C 2.3 %).

items.title: UITextView attributed text, selection and links
items.detail: `attributedText`, `selectedRange` and a painted selection, data detectors and links, `textContainer` exclusion paths, the Helvetica 12 default font, indicators after a scroll. Done 2026-10-04: attributedText runs (fonts, colours, .link) on one baseline per line without SwiftUI's two-line balancing (TextLayoutOptions.balancesTwoLines), dataDetectorTypes links opening through textView(_:shouldInteractWith:…), selectedRange painted while editing (highlight, bars and knobs), textContainer.exclusionPaths flowing lines around a path's bounds, Helvetica 12 as the default font with iOS's metrics (UIFont.installedFonts), the indicator after a drag; uikit/textview/looks with an edit step (Tier A exact, Tier C 4.6 % approximate).

items.title: UITextInput for custom text views
items.detail: The `UITextInput` protocol and `UITextInteraction` so an app's own text view can take input through the host overlay; `UIKeyInput` for the simple form.

items.title: Date picker popovers, calendars and wheels
items.detail: The calendar and time popovers a compact picker presents, `UICalendarView` and the inline style, the count-down timer, `minimumDate`/`maximumDate`, locales and calendars, `valueChanged` from the wheels; `UIPickerView` spinning by touch, custom row views, the drum's perspective (approximate, frames-only today). Done 2026-10-08: UICalendarView (the month grid from the simulator's view trees: header buttons 43.5 wide, a weekday row of equal labels from 16 in, cells of ⌊(width − 56) / 6⌋ anchored under the first label, the selection disc of the tint at 12 %, availableDateRange, single and multi-date selection), the inline style with its time row, count-down wheels with unit labels, minimum/maximum dates clamping and greying, en_GB/de/fr/ja strings and the 24-hour clock, the numeric date a narrow compact picker falls back to, wheels and picker views spun by a drag or a tap (valueChanged, didSelectRow), custom row views on the drum, a tap on a compact picker presenting the calendar or the time wheels in a popover; six new fixtures, Tier A exact, Tier C inline 1.8 %, calendar 1.1 %, locales 1.9 %, compact 1.6 % (the drums frames-only). UIColor.label is opaque black as on iOS (every text fixture moved closer to its golden).

items.title: Slider images, segment images, stepper repeat
items.detail: `UISlider` minimum and maximum images, `UISegmentedControl` images and per-segment widths, `UIStepper.autorepeat` (accepted), `UIPageControl` taps and continuous interaction.

items.title: Search results, clear button and hiding on scroll
items.detail: `searchResultsController` presented (stored today), the clear and bookmark buttons, `hidesSearchBarWhenScrolling`, `prompt` (stored), toolbar items beside a floating search field. Done 2026-10-09: the prompt's 34 pt band, the bookmark and results list buttons with their delegate calls, the search field's clear button while editing, hidesSearchBarWhenScrolling (a 0 pt band and the toolbar's platters while the content can scroll, back on a pull), an active search controller taking the navigation bar's place (the field 16 in, a dark cancel circle) with the results controller's view under it or a dim, UISearchControllerDelegate; a scroll view's offset now follows a shrinking adjusted inset, so content rises by the large title's collapse as UIKit's table does. uikit/search/looks (Tier C 1.6 %) and uikit/nav/search-results (0.5 %, activate 0.3 %; the scroll step frames-only for the blurred edges).

items.title: UIImage data, tinting and animation
items.detail: `UIImage(data:)` and `pngData()`/`jpegData()` through the host, `withTintColor`, `withRenderingMode` verified on image views, `UIImage.animatedImage` and `UIImageView.animationImages`, `UIImageView` content modes verified against the simulator. Done 2026-10-09: UIImage(data:scale:) from PNG and JPEG headers (a data URL the canvas host loads and the native painter decodes), pngData/jpegData returning the bytes, UIImage.animatedImage and UIImageView.animationImages/animationDuration/animationRepeatCount on the scene's clock (ClockAnimating shared with the spinner), rendering modes and tints and every content mode measured on the simulator (uikit/imageview/modes 0.00 %, tints 0.72 %); the real-UIKit fixture kit loads catalog images from disk (UIKitFixtureImage.named).

items.title: UIRefreshControl
items.detail: The pull-to-refresh control on scroll views and tables, its spinner (uk-spinner) and the iOS 26 geometry from the simulator. Done 2026-10-09: UIRefreshControl on scroll views and tables (UIScrollView.refreshControl): 60 tall (84.5 with a 12 pt title), eight 3.5 × 10 spokes of the label colour 5–15 from a centre 30 down, a fifth bigger and turning while refreshing, hidden at rest; refreshing adds the control's height to the adjusted inset so the content rests under it; a pull released past 60 begins refreshing and sends valueChanged, beginRefreshing sends nothing; uikit/scroll/refresh with refreshing and ended steps, Tier A exact, Tier C 0.5 / 1.2 / 0.5 %.

items.title: Zooming, inset adjustment and scroll-to-top
items.detail: `viewForZooming` with pinch and `zoomScale`, `.automatic`'s extra rules inside navigation controllers (the safe-area adjustment is done), `keyboardDismissMode`, scroll-to-top on a status bar tap, `scrollIndicatorInsets`. Done 2026-10-09: zooming (viewForZooming scaled about the content's origin with the content size following, setZoomScale, zoom(to:), a pinch about its centre, isZooming and the zoom callbacks; uikit/scroll/zoom 0.2 %), .automatic adjusting a view controller's first scroll view even when short (uikit/nav/scroll-inset 0.6 %), keyboardDismissMode resigning on a drag, UIKitScene.scrollToTop() for the status bar tap with scrollsToTop and the delegate's say, vertical/horizontal indicator insets replacing the 3 pt margins; Tier A exact, Tier B passing.

items.title: UIPageViewController
items.detail: Scroll and page-curl-as-scroll transition styles, the data source and delegate, the page indicator. Done 2026-10-09: the scroll style's paging slots widened by the inter-page spacing (uikit/page/scroll: −10 … 330, the indicator 74 × 26 at (123, 374)), neighbours loaded as a drag begins and settled on with the delegate's callbacks, setViewControllers, the page control's taps, the page-curl style as a scroll (uikit/page/curl); Tier A exact, Tier C 0.2 %. Open: the curl animation, spreads.

items.title: UISplitViewController
items.detail: The column styles, display modes and the compact collapse; the iPad geometry from a simulator of that idiom.

items.title: Table view corners
items.detail: The grouped (non-inset) style's geometry, the `RowAnimation` kinds (every animation fades and slides today), swipe button widths and fonts, the lifted row's shadow, the tracking background while touched, `imageProperties`, catalog images in list content (the UIKit harness has no asset catalog), sidebar and `plainHeader` appearances, right-to-left.

items.title: Collection view corners
items.detail: Estimated dimensions in compositional layouts, item supplementary items, `groupPagingCentered`, `visibleItemsInvalidationHandler`, decorations in orthogonal sections, pinned footers, the scroll pocket blur, drag reordering, `UICollectionViewLayout` animation hooks, the diffable move detection when an item also changes section, outline disclosure options and reordering, the sidebar appearance.

items.title: UIVisualEffectView and the glass
items.detail: Blur and vibrancy effects as a display-list filter group over what lies beneath (the painters have blur); the iOS 26 glass in bars and the scroll pocket is a tint today. The floating tab bar over coloured content is opaque where iOS 26's glass tints what lies beneath (ios/representable/hostingsafearea-tabs is approximate, 5.6 %). Done 2026-10-09: the substrate's backdropBlur command (a Gaussian of the painted ground within a path, saturated on request; native snapshot blur, canvas filter), UIVisualEffectView/UIBlurEffect/UIVibrancyEffect with sigmas and tints fitted to every style over four grounds (uikit/view/materials 1.1 %), the glass platters and the SwiftUI tab capsule blurring their ground under white at 31 % with the selected lens translucent (ios/representable/hostingsafearea-tabs 5.6 → 2.3 %). Open: vibrancy blending, the refraction and rim, the dark tints.

items.title: Layer corners, borders and shadows against pixels
items.detail: The painted corners (continuous too), borders and shadows of `uikit/view/*` compared with the simulator's pixels; the fixtures are frames-only where the look is unverified. Done 2026-10-09: every element of uikit/view/layers matched within edge antialiasing (0.2 %), and uikit/view/looks (0.3 %) adds shadowPath (painted in the background colour), shadow colour, hairline and thick borders on rounded and capsule corners, a continuous bordered corner, the unclamped corner lens CoreAnimation draws past half a side, group opacity, and CAShapeLayer masks through the substrate's mask group.

items.title: Trait overrides and observation
items.detail: `overrideUserInterfaceStyle` on a view (the window's and `traitOverrides` work), `registerForTraitChanges` and `traitCollectionDidChange` on every change, size classes from the host size, dark samples of the wheels and of presentations other than the alert. Done 2026-10-09: overrideUserInterfaceStyle and traitOverrides on views measured (uikit/view/traits 1.2 %: dark islands on a light page, a light one inside a dark one), trait changes from every path reaching traitCollectionDidChange and registerForTraitChanges observers on views and view controllers, size classes from the host size (compact wide under 500, compact tall under 400), nine dark samples (inline calendar, calendar view, wheels, materials with their dark tints fitted, sheet, popover, refresh, image tints, looks) all within tolerance.

items.title: UIAppearance proxies
items.detail: `appearance()` and `appearance(whenContainedInInstancesOf:)` applied when a view enters a window.

items.title: Gradient and text layers, display links, animation options
items.detail: `CAGradientLayer`, `CATextLayer`, `CADisplayLink` on the scene's clock, `CAAnimationGroup` playback, keyframes through every value, additive animations, `repeat`/`autoreverse`/`beginFromCurrentState` on `UIView.animate` (accepted), `delayFactor`, `scrubsLinearly` and spring velocity on property animators.

items.title: Layout guides, animated constraints and stacks
items.detail: Frames of app-made `UILayoutGuide`s, constraint changes animated by `layoutIfNeeded` inside `UIView.animate`, hugging defaults per control verified, `UIStackView.fillProportionally` and overflow compression against UIKit, spacing after hidden views, solver performance on large trees.

items.title: Blend modes, attributed drawing and CGPath
items.detail: `setBlendMode` and `UIImage.draw` with blend modes (accepted), antialiasing switches and `clear`, per-range attributes with underline and strikethrough, `NSMutableAttributedString`, `CGPath`/`CGMutablePath` on Apple platforms, caching drawn content between frames.

items.title: Hardware keyboard and the focus system
items.detail: `UIKeyCommand` on responders, `pressesBegan`/`pressesEnded`, `UIFocusSystem` with the focus ring for keyboard navigation across controls, table and collection cells.

items.title: Drag and drop interactions
items.detail: `UIDragInteraction`/`UIDropInteraction`, the table and collection drag and drop delegates over the runtime's drag session (SwiftUI's `draggable` shares it).

items.title: Accessibility notifications and custom actions
items.detail: `UIAccessibility.post`, `accessibilityCustomActions`, `accessibilityElements` ordering, `isAccessibilityElement` and traits verified against the overlay the SwiftUI walk produces; a VoiceOver pass over Examples/UIKitSettings.

items.title: UIPasteboard
items.detail: `UIPasteboard.general` over the runtime pasteboard and the host clipboard writer SwiftUI's `copyable` uses.

items.title: Scenes and app lifecycle
items.detail: `UIWindowScene`, `UISceneDelegate` and `UIApplication` lifecycle notifications from page visibility and activation; several windows in the host; `UIFeedbackGenerator` as no-ops.

items.title: Trim the wasm bundle: Foundation
items.detail: Asked for 300 KB of headroom under the 3 MB budget by trimming the symbol and font tables; the tables measured 60 KB brotli and the cost was FoundationEssentials, whose members link whole (6.3 MB raw for a `Calendar`). Decision 0017: the `WebFoundation` module's stand-ins for `Data`, `URL`, `Calendar`, `TimeZone`, `Locale`, `DateComponents`, `IndexPath` and the sort comparators shadow FoundationEssentials' on wasm; Counter 3.05 MB to about 2.1 MB brotli, UIKitCounter 2.24 MB to 1.46 MB.

items.title: WebFoundation's gaps against Foundation
items.detail: The wasm stand-ins (decision 0017) cover what the frameworks and ordinary apps call. Missing: `String.Encoding` and `String(data:encoding:)`, `URLComponents` and international host names, named time zones and daylight saving (`TimeZone.current` is the browser's fixed offset), calendars other than proleptic Gregorian, `DateFormatter` and `FormatStyle`, `wrappingComponents`, `Data` slices that keep their indices. Grow them as apps hit them; each FoundationEssentials type used instead costs the whole library.

items.title: Storyboards and nibs
items.detail: Interface Builder archives are undocumented binary formats; apps port their scenes to code. Non-goal.

items.title: Linux: build, CI, painter and host
items.detail: The native headless build and tests are supported on Linux with Swift 6.3.3, alongside wasm cross-compilation. Remaining: a Skia or Cairo painter, a GTK window and the WebKitGTK host.

items.title: Native text selection, IME and windows
items.detail: A caret and selection painted inside the text (the browser's for now), IME marked text, several real windows, the menu bar and window commands, file dialogs, opening bundles by double click in Tools/Host.

items.title: IME, autofill and VoiceOver by hand
items.detail: Japanese and Chinese IMEs and Safari autofill through the overlay input (spike 0.12's risk), a VoiceOver session in Safari; the findings recorded per browser in the matrix.

items.title: First frame and large lists
items.detail: The gallery and progress bundles' first frame on a slow connection, laziness in lists and lazy stacks (sw-lazy, sw-list-looks), a frame budget probe in CI over Examples/Landing.
